environment.description: Spring Boot 2.7.x deployed on EKS with ElastiCache Redis 6.x as cache backend. Service is behind an internal NLB (Layer 4) with no request inspection. Redis instance is in the same VPC subnet with security group allowing port 6379 from any pod in the cluster namespace. No Redis AUTH configured. Cache key is derived from attacker-controlled HTTP headers (X-Token-Id and X-Signature-Hash). HSM is AWS CloudHSM but the cache poisoning attack does not require key material access.

config.cache: ElastiCache Redis 6.2, no AUTH, no TLS
config.network: NLB (L4 only), no WAF, no request header validation
config.redis_access: Security group allows 6379 from 10.0.0.0/16 (entire VPC CIDR)
